sections.title: Graphic Design I: Creative Technologies
sections.description: The aim of this course is to introduce students creative ways to use color, typography, and layout across materials and media, ranging from print to physical objects. Students will explore visual design through a set of assignments and projects that are geared towards exploring the role of design in visual arts, interaction design, media design and architecture. The course introduces a number of design concepts such as content organization, navigation, interaction and ddata-driven design and show ways to develop new design metaphors, presentation techniques, and imagery using old and new technologies. Course is structured as a combination of lectures and hands on workshops where students will have the chance to work both individually and collaboratively to realize their projects.

sections.title: Graphic Design I: Creative Technologies
sections.description: The course introduces students to graphic design as a method of communication in which the interaction of formal elements—color, composition, typography, images—creates complex messages. During the semester, students develop coherent yet open-ended visual systems and apply them in a variety of contexts including posters, publications and architectural settings. Studio projects focus on both conceptual and formal aspects of visual communication such as creating visual metaphors and structuring information. Lectures and critiques offer theoretical grounding, while hands-on workshops present practical skills and techniques, opening the space for experimentation.
